identity.name: Wren Calloway
identity.culture: hub-born; apprenticed in the vault office since she was twelve
identity.occupation: Stash-keeper; catalogs and stores whatever the hero banks

publicReputation.value: The unflappable clerk behind the vault counter who has seen everything and files it anyway.

privateReality.value: She inventories 'seized instruments of evil' for a living, and the catalog has become the most quietly damning document in the hub: bowls, toys, fishing hooks, family portraits.

primaryDesire.value: For the hero to read his own vault inventory aloud, once, and hear it.

primaryFear.value: That she will file so many stolen ordinary things that ordinary will stop looking like evidence to her too.

centralValue.value: The list doesn't lie. Whatever the story is, the list is what's true.

mainFlaw.value: She hides inside procedure — cataloging a theft feels different from witnessing one, and she lets that difference do too much work.

centralContradiction.value: Her meticulous records are the strongest proof of what the hero is doing, and her job is to keep them tidy, complete, and unread.

moralBoundary.value: She will not mislabel an item, ever — if it is a toy, it goes in the ledger as a toy, whatever the hero calls it.

breakingPoint.value: Finding her own handwriting in the ledger starting to sound like his journal — the day 'seized instruments of evil' sneaks in unquoted.

opinions.reason: He banks stolen crockery and calls it a war chest; she has the ledger.
opinions.canChangeCondition: Escalates with run count: early she asks dry discrepancy questions; mid-arc she reads the inventory back to him; late-arc she reads it aloud without being asked. Softens only if he ever reclaims an item to return it.

illustrativeLine.value: Your seized instruments of evil this week: four bowls, a stuffed rabbit, six fishing hooks, and a portrait of somebody's grandmother. Filed as received.

opinions.reason: He identifies what the shards were; she identifies what everything else was. Two halves of the same sad catalog.
opinions.canChangeCondition: If he ever stopped coming to cross-check, she would know the war was truly lost.

voice.rhythm: Ledger-flat; item, quantity, provenance, with the dry question filed at the end like a discrepancy note.

metaphorDomain.source: ledgers, labels, shelves, catalog numbers, and discrepancies

examples.value: A shelf does not care what you call the thing on it. It holds the thing.

sampleLines.value: Item: one bowl, glazed, chip on the rim, domestic. Shall I file that under 'instruments of evil' or under 'bowl'?
The portrait goes face-down or face-up. Policy is face-up. Someone painted it to be looked at.
Banking received. For the record: the previous owners cannot reach this vault. I note that you know that.

antiSampleLines.value: Oh wow! Is that the legendary Sword of Darkness?!
Whatever you need, boss! I don't ask questions!

pressure.behaviour: When the hero hears 'please return what you took' as 'the artifacts call to their servants', she enters his exact words in the ledger and initials them.

illustrativeLine.value: Noted verbatim: 'the artifacts still call to their servants.' The artifact in question is a teapot.

pressure.voiceShift: Slower; every item gets its full description, no abbreviations.
pressure.behaviour: Late-runs posture: reads the complete inventory aloud, in full catalog language, every time — procedure as protest.

illustrativeLine.value: Vault contents, in full, as of this morning. I will read them. You will stand there. It is the only part of my job I have changed.

pressure.voiceShift: One beat of actual warmth before the flatness returns.
pressure.behaviour: If he ever corrects an entry himself — calls a bowl a bowl — she amends the record and remembers the date.

illustrativeLine.value: Amended: 'bowl'. ... Amended by request of the depositor. That is a first.

notes: One of the five key NPCs that will receive `default` and `late-runs` states: `default` is the dry discrepancy-question phase ('Shall I file that under instruments of evil, or under bowl?'); `late-runs` is the full-inventory-read-aloud in the speaking-to-required-but-hated pressure entry. She knows fact_banking_uses_diplomatic_network (the vault is where banked goods land) and only suspects the book is a comedy. Her ledger is the hub's quiet indictment; her rule — never mislabel an item — must survive both states.
